newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER FINDS BAYERN CHAIRMANSHIP A STRAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER FINDS BAYERN CHAIRMANSHIP A STRAIN.

text.p: Franz Beckenbauer said on Tuesday he often thought of quitting as chairman of German champions Bayern Munich but would probably stay on and juggle the job with his many other commitments.

"I often ask myself questions. It's a benevolent job and I don't have enough time to be as effective as I would want to be," said Beckenbauer, who is with one of his chief sponsors at the Tournoi de France 1998 World Cup dress rehearsal.

"In December there are (club presidential) elections. It's my choice, but a lot of people at the club are asking me to carry on," added the former Bayern and German captain in an informal chat with journalists.
He said that as far as he knew there was no rival for the chairmanship of the German championship club.

Beckenbauer played down the hint that he could quit in an article signed by him in the German newspaper Bild in which he wrote: "The chairmanship of a Bundesliga club, with a turnover of more than 100 million marks ($58 million) requires the whole man. That's why I'm thinking what my next move is."
He added in the article: "Must I carry on searching my soul for three days every time we lose?"
But in the relaxed atmosphere of a Lyon restaurant, it was evident that Beckenbauer enjoys the work and is proud to have presided over Bayern's record 14th championship this season.

He went on to compare Bayern with some of the world's biggest clubs, like Barcelona, in terms of internal problems like player conflicts, notably that between present and former German captains Juergen Klinsmann and Lothar Matthaeus.
Beckenbauer, who guided his country to their third World Cup in Italy in 1990, denied wanting a move upwards to the presidency of the German federation or even a return to the field as coach.
"I don't have the feeling for it (coaching) any more," said the man who became known as the Kaiser for his elegant, commanding style of play.
"When we were in Vienna once, a photograper asked me to pose beside a bust of Kaiser Franz Josef and that's when the name came into use," he said.
Beckenbauer confirmed Bayern's interest in France defender Bixente Lizarazu, especially since they have sold Christian Ziege to AC Milan.
"But Athletic Bilbao want to keep him," he said.

He said Brazilian Giovane Elber was the replacement for the departing Klinsmann, but he had no other clues as to Bayern's recruiting plans for an assault on the European Cup next season except to say there were promising youngsters itching for their chance in the first team.
"All that is done at management level," Beckenbauer said.
But he added that Bayern were pleased with Italian coach Giovanni Trappatoni and hoped to persuade him to extend his contract which expires at the end of next season.
The current success of German clubs -- Borussia Dortmund winning the European Cup and Schalke the UEFA Cup -- was down simply to the age-old German tenet of arbeit, work.
"German players are not better than French, for instance, there's nothing special. It may not always be terribly elegant, it's just work, work, work."
